historical_references.reference: Saint Camillus de Lellis (1550-1614) was an Italian priest and the founder of the Brothers of the Common Life and the Ministers of the Sick. He is often considered the patron saint of nurses, paramedics, and camerlengos (chamberlains).

Saint Camillus of Jericho (circa 333-374 AD) was a Syrian monk and hermit, who is traditionally believed to have been the first to care for the sick and the lepers. The story of his healing of a leper is one of the earliest examples of Christian charity and compassion.
